name: Resource Dialog Composition
description: Composes an independently owned compact Dialog header and footer around a Workbench resource form with native submission semantics.

states: Open Rename from a Project menu and inspect the lightweight compact title that also labels the only field, without a description, and the footer actions.

Open the simple Project path or Tab title form and compare the same structure with a dense description, a normal-weight field label, and Esc and Enter hints on the actions whose keys remain unambiguous throughout the task.

useWhen: A compact Workbench resource has passed repository modal admission and needs a titled form with confirm or cancel actions.
The form must share the established dialog body, footer, cancellation, validation, and submission structure.
avoidWhen: The workflow needs a full-page editor, multistep navigation, or a persistent inspector surface.
A destructive decision only needs the shared anchored or modal confirmation pattern without editable fields.
invariants: The Dialog header and footer own shell hierarchy and actions independently from the form body; the form never encloses or restyles the shell header.
The title and any decision-relevant description explain the resource and outcome before the first editable field.

Every consumer uses the compact Desktop form-Dialog typography hierarchy: a lightweight compact heading, dense normal-weight supporting copy, normal-weight control text, code typography only for exact paths, commands, or other code-like values, and subordinate key hints.

Every editable field has a persistent visible compact label, which for a Dialog's only field may be a title that names its value; supporting and error text uses the body role, contextual descriptions appear only when validation or platform limits matter, and placeholders never replace guidance.
Cancel and submit preserve native form semantics; their buttons expose aria-hidden Kbd hints only while Escape and Enter retain those exact unambiguous meanings throughout the editable task.
